scheme_name: Primary Cooperative Agriculture and Rural Development Bank: For Plantation (Tea)
description:
The Primary Cooperative Agriculture and Rural Development Bank for Plantation (Tea) is a specialized financial institution established to promote the development of tea plantations in India.

This scheme was launched in 1978 under the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare.

The primary objective of this scheme is to provide financial assistance to small and marginal farmers engaged in tea cultivation.

The scheme aims to enhance the productivity and profitability of tea plantations through various financial support mechanisms.

The government has set a measurable target of increasing the area under tea cultivation by 10 percent over the next five years.

Additionally, the scheme seeks to improve the quality of tea produced by providing access to modern agricultural practices and technologies.

The benefits under this scheme include financial assistance in the form of loans for the establishment and maintenance of tea plantations.

Farmers can avail loans up to INR 10 lakh for the establishment of new tea gardens.

The interest rate on these loans is subsidized at 4 percent per annum.

The repayment period for these loans is typically set at 5 to 7 years, depending on the project size and scope.

Farmers are also eligible for additional benefits such as training programs on best practices in tea cultivation.

These training programs are conducted by agricultural universities and research institutions across the country.

To be eligible for this scheme, applicants must be small or marginal farmers with land holdings not exceeding 5 acres.

The annual income of the applicant should not exceed INR 2 lakh to qualify for the financial assistance.

Applicants must also possess a valid land title or lease agreement for the land intended for tea cultivation.

The application process involves several steps to ensure that only eligible candidates receive assistance.

Interested farmers must first approach their local Primary Cooperative Agriculture and Rural Development Bank.

They need to fill out the application form and submit it along with the required documents.

Required documents include proof of identity such as an Aadhar card or voter ID.

Farmers must also provide land ownership documents and income certificates.

Once the application is submitted, the bank will conduct a verification process.

This process includes site visits and assessments to confirm the applicant's eligibility.

After verification, the bank will process the loan application and communicate the decision to the applicant.

If approved, the loan amount will be disbursed in installments based on the project milestones.

Disbursement typically occurs within 30 days of loan approval.

The frequency of loan disbursement is aligned with the agricultural calendar to support farmers during critical planting and harvesting periods.

The implementing authority for this scheme is the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare.

The scheme is executed through a network of Primary Cooperative Agriculture and Rural Development Banks located in various states.

Each bank operates under the guidelines set forth by the National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development.

Farmers can contact their local bank branches for assistance and further information.

The scheme has been instrumental in improving the livelihoods of tea farmers across India.

According to the Tea Board of India, tea cultivation employs over 1.5 million people directly.

The scheme has also contributed to the increase in tea production, which reached approximately 1.3 million metric tons in the 2021-2022 fiscal year.

The government has allocated INR 500 crore for the financial year 2022-2023 to support this initiative.

This funding is aimed at providing loans and subsidies to enhance the productivity of tea plantations.

The scheme also includes provisions for the development of infrastructure related to tea processing and marketing.

Farmers are encouraged to form cooperatives to enhance their bargaining power in the market.

The cooperative model allows farmers to pool resources and share knowledge for better productivity.

The government provides additional incentives for cooperatives that achieve significant milestones in productivity.

These incentives can include additional financial support and recognition at state and national levels.

The scheme also emphasizes sustainable agricultural practices to ensure environmental conservation.

Farmers are trained in organic farming techniques and integrated pest management.

This approach not only improves tea quality but also enhances the sustainability of tea cultivation.

The government monitors the impact of the scheme through regular assessments and feedback from beneficiaries.

This feedback is crucial for making necessary adjustments to the scheme to better serve the needs of farmers.

The scheme has seen a steady increase in participation since its inception.

In the last five years, the number of beneficiaries has increased by 20 percent annually.

The government aims to further increase this participation rate by enhancing outreach programs.

Awareness campaigns are conducted to inform farmers about the benefits and procedures of the scheme.

These campaigns are often held in collaboration with local agricultural departments and NGOs.

The scheme also aligns with the broader goals of the National Mission on Sustainable Agriculture.

This mission aims to promote sustainable agricultural practices across various sectors, including tea cultivation.

The integration of technology in tea farming is another focus area under this scheme.

Farmers are encouraged to adopt modern techniques such as drip irrigation and precision farming.

These technologies help in optimizing resource use and increasing yields.

The scheme also supports research and development initiatives related to tea cultivation.

Partnerships with agricultural universities and research institutions are established to foster innovation.

This collaborative approach ensures that farmers have access to the latest advancements in tea cultivation.

Overall, the Primary Cooperative Agriculture and Rural Development Bank for Plantation (Tea) scheme represents a significant effort by the Indian government to support tea farmers.

By providing financial assistance and promoting sustainable practices, the scheme aims to enhance the livelihoods of millions of farmers involved in tea cultivation.

The ongoing commitment of the government to this sector is evident through continued investments and policy support.

Farmers are encouraged to take advantage of this scheme to improve their productivity and income levels.

The success of the scheme is crucial for the overall growth of the tea industry in India.
